meta.title: Membrii GYW
meta.channel: Grow your WEALTH - Valentin Dragu si Alex Marian
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · Jensen Huang exit and the semis rotation · CoreWeave/Nebius and the bond market · SoftBank's pledged ARM stake · Anthropic IPO math vs SpaceX · Fed, Iran and the City of London · defensives, Hims and Supermicro

snapshot: Jensen Huang's resignation is treated as a market event, not gossip: Dragu sees money leaving Nvidia for **AMD and Broadcom** and hitting Nvidia-linked names like Nebius.
Nvidia at about **$4 trillion** after the drop: Dragu calls it undervalued on multiples but late in its growth cycle; growth investors are handing it to value investors.
CoreWeave reported well (backlog about **$100B**, up from about $70B) but its debt traded near **15%**; Nebius jumped 16-18% on the print.
SoftBank posted a **$7B** net loss; about 70% of its portfolio sits in ARM and OpenAI, and the pledged ARM shares could be margin-called.
Anthropic IPO at about **$78/share**, targeting $1.2-1.4T and raising $60-80B; Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft and TSMC lined up as anchor buyers.
Fed: a **0.25** hike in December is priced and seen as unavoidable; a 0.5 hike is called alarmist.
Defensive rotation into Costco, Walmart, Coca-Cola and Pepsi; Dragu would sell Costco's buyback pop and rotate into Google.
Romania: pressure on the leu, weaker remittances, and foreign investment parked waiting for Ukraine reconstruction.

themes.title: Jensen Huang's exit pushes semis money from Nvidia to AMD and Broadcom
themes.lead: Dragu reads the departure as a durable hit to Nvidia's valuation that benefits AMD and Broadcom and drags Nvidia-dependent names.
bullets: Dragu has been adding to **Broadcom**; he also holds Nebius, which he says is hit despite a strong report because of its Nvidia ties.
Nvidia's index weight touches ETFs, 401(k)s and pension funds, so the impact is "very hard", not one man's mistake quickly forgotten.
Nvidia market cap about $4T; Alex Marian sees maybe $6T upside (~50%), arguing semis peers carry less risk for the same exposure.
Dragu: Nvidia trades at a very low multiple, but semis growth has 3-4 more quarters before the market prices decelerating growth (40% to 36% to 32%).
The stock is moving from growth investors to value investors, who "negotiate everything" like an apartment buyer haggling below the cheapest listing.
Example of a good company at a bad price: buy Nvidia near $230 and a consolidation at $140-170 leaves you down 20-25% for a long time.
Huang owns about 3.5-3.6% of Nvidia; Elon Musk said he'd hire him, and the hosts muse a SpaceX-for-Nvidia share swap.

themes.title: CoreWeave's strong print meets a bond market charging 15%
themes.lead: Both neoclouds reported well; the risk sits in the credit market, where CoreWeave's borrowing costs and default insurance have jumped.
bullets: CoreWeave backlog rose to about **$100B** from about $70B (contracts signed in advance).
Its traded loans yield around 15%, which weighs on future borrowing; rising Treasury yields raise the cost of convertibles and senior notes.
Default insurance on CoreWeave debt has climbed sharply; lenders are paying up to hedge.
Nebius rose **16-18%** right after CoreWeave's report; Dragu calls its balance sheet much stronger than CoreWeave's.
Nebius stopped giving forward guidance, but both firms have large prepaid contracts.

quote.text: Corewave, Nebius sunt niste companii fara de care nu se poate dezvolta AI-ul pe mai departe.

themes.title: SoftBank's pledged ARM shares are a margin call waiting for a further drop
themes.lead: With about 70% of the portfolio in ARM and OpenAI and ARM shares pledged for loans, SoftBank is hoping, and hope is not a strategy.
bullets: SoftBank reported a **$7B** net loss, mostly unrealised, after ARM's fall.
It pledged ARM (and OpenAI) shares to banks to borrow and invest more in OpenAI; Dragu thinks the pledge level is around $280-300+ per ARM share, but isn't sure.
Alex Marian puts a further 25-35% ARM drop as the trigger for forced cuts; Dragu says selling would just push ARM lower and invite execution by the banks.
Masayoshi Son built his record on near-zero-rate yen swapped into dollars; he lost 70-80% on SoFi, which the hosts made 300% on.
Dragu would have preferred Son bet on SpaceX or even Anthropic over OpenAI.
Their view of Son: at the end of his career he wants to make history, not be right, which makes him dangerous with other people's money.

quote.text: Speranta nu e o strategie in piata de capital.

themes.title: Anthropic's IPO keeps the AI money flowing, but it won't outshine SpaceX
themes.lead: Its backers need a successful listing to mark up their stakes; the hosts doubt the hype and rank SpaceX's IPO far above it.
bullets: Pricing about **$78/share**, targeting $1.2-1.4T market cap and raising $60-80B; valuation talk fell from $2T to $1-1.2T within a month.
Amazon: about $18B invested, about **15x** gain, stake worth about $271B; Google: about $33B invested plus $10B at the IPO, stake about $139B.
Announced IPO buyers: Google $10B, Nvidia $10B, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom and Microsoft about $1B each, TSMC $500M.
Dragu: a successful listing sustains AI investment; a weak one makes banks and VC funds ask whether to keep funding AI, risking a big AI correction.
Dragu would have delayed the listing to summer 2027, as he says Sam Altman did with OpenAI.
Alex Marian cites an IPO watcher who can't see the hype: Claude Code writing code is real productivity, but the AI-replaces-everything fear is overdone.
AI products commoditise in 4-6 months (Chinese or US rivals make today's paid feature free), while each new model needs costlier Nvidia/AMD compute.
Next, Alex expects OpenAI to list sooner than expected, pulling liquidity from wherever Anthropic investors take profits.

themes.title: A 0.25 December hike is baked in; Iran keeps oil and inflation in play
themes.lead: Without October CPI (data not collected during last year's shutdown), producer prices become the inflation signal; the hosts rule out a 0.5 hike.
bullets: Prices already include a **0.25** December hike; speculation about 0.5 is called alarmist, and Dragu says a hike can't be avoided.
What matters more is the post-decision statement; Warsh presents a committee vote, not his own decision.
December tax-loss selling expected in retail favourites bought at the top (SanDisk near $2,000, Micron near $1,100), and in Nike at funds.
Iran: a fragile ceasefire Trump claims after Qatar talks; Iran struck an island near Oman with US bases and more tankers were hit in Hormuz on Thursday.
Dragu argues the Hormuz conflict serves hidden City of London banking interests tied to Middle East oil since British Petroleum, and won't end until those are settled.

quote.text: De un 0,25 nu cred ca scapam.

themes.watch: The City of London thesis is Dragu's own; he acknowledges it sounds conspiratorial and gives no specifics.

themes.title: Sell Costco's buyback pop, skip Hims, stay away from Supermicro
themes.lead: Defensives are drawing money, but Dragu would rotate out into corrected tech and avoid momentum names with clouds over them.
bullets: Costco: solid report, special dividend, new **$4B** buyback; Dragu would take the pop and rebalance into Google, which he sees rising in H2 2027 and 2028.
Costco, Target and Walmart benefit from tariff refunds; weak retailer numbers now mean low expectations to beat later.
Hims & Hers: weak results; the Novo Nordisk dispute looks like the break point and FTC ad scrutiny is a risk; Dragu would rank it among investors' last options.
Better corrected alternatives: Caterpillar, Google and Walmart; Oscar named as a health stock with less risk than Hims.
Supermicro: the US charged a person over smuggling Nvidia chips through it; Dragu feels vindicated for keeping members away.
Rallies in a clouded stock can be exit liquidity: institutions sell into retail FOMO, then dump.

takeaways.title: Wait for Nvidia to find support before buying; look at Broadcom and AMD for the same exposure.
Watch CoreWeave's bond yields and default insurance, not just its backlog.
Treat SoftBank as a levered ARM/OpenAI bet that depends on a 2027 OpenAI IPO.
Take profits on defensive pops like Costco and rotate into corrected tech such as Google.
Be wary of rallies in clouded stocks like Supermicro: they can be exit liquidity.

claims.claim: The Fed hikes by 0.25 in December; a 0.5 hike is very unlikely.
Semis can keep growing 3-4 quarters before the market prices a deceleration.
A Nvidia consolidation at $140-170 would leave buyers near $230 down 20-25% for a long time.
SoftBank could close its doors if things go wrong in 2027 and OpenAI lacks a resounding IPO.
A further 25-35% ARM drop could force SoftBank to cut its ARM position.
SpaceX returns to about $200 per share easily at some point.
Google rises substantially in the second half of 2027 and 2028.
Tesla and SpaceX would each fall about 60% if Elon Musk left.
Ukraine reconstruction draws large investment within one to two years, at Romania's expense for now.

other_news.title: Dragu expects no improvement this year or next, with pressure on the leu, falling remittances from Romanians abroad, and big foreign budgets waiting for Ukraine reconstruction.
Dragu claims the Anthropic-driven fears (cybersecurity and software being wiped out) haven't played out: cybersecurity stocks sit at record highs.
